purpose: Draws and edits the Description of a Plan card as one record per Keyword part in a tree: add a part, edit its text and source, paste many parts at once, move a part up, down, in or out by buttons, keys or drag, and remove a part with its sub-parts, all written in one queue so the order of the writes is kept, with every read and write supplied by the host.
namedChanges: Imports (lines 5-90): `PlanButtonRow` from `plan-button-row`; `DescriptionHelp` from `description-help`; `FieldRow` from `field-row`; `modalIsOpen` and `insideOpenLayer` from `open-popups`; `SortableTree`, `TreeItem`, `flattenTree`, `DropTarget` from `sortable-tree`; `useCardMode` from `card-mode`; `PlanSource` from `plan-source`; `planTypePair` from `plan-kinds`; `duplicateTagSentence`, `isTypeName`, `linkAddress`, `recordTag` from `plan-links-model`; `indexBefore`, `planPartialWrite`, `removalPlan`, `REMOVAL_TOO_DEEP`, `REMOVAL_TOO_MANY` and the types `Gone`, `Kept`, `LevelMovePlan`, `PartialTarget` from `description-parts-model`, and every part rule the file used (`ASSUMPTION_ELEMENT`, `ASSUMPTION_WARNING`, `assumptionHedge`, `descriptionTree`, `asGrid`, `dropPlan`, `isAssumptionPart`, `keywordProblem`, `moveInPlan`, `moveOutPlan`, `nextOrder`, `partBody`, `partKeyword`, `partOrder`, `previewPaste`, `reorderPlan`, `stepPlan`, `suggestKeyword`, `tagTaken`, `DescriptionNode`, `OrderChange`, `PastePart`); `planSourceEqual`, `readLineSources`, `rowServedFact`, `sameServedList`, `sourceWithStatedBy`, `writeLineSource`, `PlanSourceValue` from `plan-card-facts`; `BaseRecord`, `GridRecord` from `base-record`. Each was compared with the source's own, comments stripped (a script reads both and prints the same declaration): all are the same, except `isTypeName`, which is the `type-key` unit's (the source's compares with the app's type registry; `type-key` has the same result when the registry knows no type, and a host with a registry calls `setTypeKey`).

`@tanstack/react-query` is gone: `useQueryClient()` is not called (the query client stays in the host), and each `qc.*` call, query key and cache helper is a host member (see above). `reReadLevels` takes the host where it took the query client; `planPartialWrite` and `removalPlan` take the host (which contains the level members) where they took it. `planFindKey` and `planRecordKey` are not in the unit: the host forms its own keys from the arguments.

Each host call is made with the same arguments, in the same place and order as the source's call, but for what the key did: `qc.getQueryData(planFindKey(planVault, "a:partOf", id))` is `host.getFind(planVault, "a:partOf", id)` (the `const own = planFindKey(...)` line is gone); `qc.setQueryData(planFindKey(...), v)` is `host.setFind(planVault, "a:partOf", id, v)`; `qc.getQueriesData({ queryKey: ["plan-find", planVault] })` iterated as `[, data]` is `host.getFinds(planVault)` iterated as `data`; `qc.setQueryData(planRecordKey(id, uri), row)` is `host.setRecordRead(id, uri, row)`; the `qc.getQueryData(recordsKey(id))?.pages.flatMap(...) ?? []` expression is `host.cachedRecords(id)`; `useDeleteRecord(vaultId)` is `host.useDeleteRecord?.(vaultId)` and `del.mutateAsync` is `del!.mutateAsync`; the writers are called with a `!` after the member; `e instanceof RecordConflictError` is `host.isConflict(e)` (three places in `patchPart` and the two source and text handlers); `<HelpButton>` is `<host.HelpButton>`.
The view reads `host` from the new `DescriptionPartsHostContext` (`useDescriptionPartsHost`, private) first; with no provider it throws.
One added line, before `useCardMode()`: `if (!(host.createRecord && host.patchRecord && host.useDeleteRecord)) canEdit = false;`. That is the read-only behaviour: the same as `canEdit` false.

Kept inside, as in the source: the write queue (`run` on `tail`), `syncTree`, the move and removal plans, the focus-after-move effect, the document `mousedown` and Escape effects, `focusTagInput`, `onBindAdd` called on every render, `selfRef` (the latest person on every render). The comments are the source's.

library.title: Description editor (Keyword parts)
library.note: Draws and edits the Description as a tree of parts; the pure model is description-parts-model, the drag tree sortable-tree.
